title: A Podcast on Healthy Habits
description: Four recordings about healthy habits: a sleep interview, a talk about food and water, friends planning to run and a community centre announcement.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · Sleep
parts.intro: You will hear a podcast host, Ben, talking to a sleep expert, Dr Lopez.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Welcome to Better Days, the podcast about small changes that improve your life. I'm Ben, and today I'm talking with Dr Lopez, who studies sleep. Dr Lopez, why does sleep matter so much?

script.speaker: Dr Lopez
script.text: Well, Ben, while we sleep, our body repairs itself and our brain stores what we learned that day. Students who sleep badly often forget what they studied.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: How many hours do we need?

script.speaker: Dr Lopez
script.text: Teenagers need about nine hours, and adults need seven or eight. But the time you go to bed matters too. Going to bed at the same time every night is more important than a very long sleep at the weekend.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: I'm guilty of sleeping until noon on Sundays!

script.speaker: Dr Lopez
script.text: Many people do, but it confuses your body clock. On Monday you feel as if you've flown across the world.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: What about phones? I always scroll in bed.

script.speaker: Dr Lopez
script.text: That's the biggest problem. The light wakes up your brain. I suggest switching off screens an hour before bed and reading a real book instead.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: And caffeine?

script.speaker: Dr Lopez
script.text: No coffee or strong tea after three in the afternoon. For some people even a cup at noon is too late.

parts.title: Part 2 · Food and drink
parts.intro: You will hear a presenter, Maya, talking about healthy eating habits.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: Hello again, this is Maya, and today's habit is about food and drink. Don't worry, I'm not going to tell you to give up chocolate.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: Let's start with water. Most of us don't drink enough. A simple trick is to put a full bottle on your desk each morning, and finish it by the afternoon. I did this for one month, and my headaches almost disappeared.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: Next, breakfast. Some people say it is the most important meal of the day, but the truth is more complicated. What matters is eating something with protein, such as eggs or yoghurt, rather than just sugary cereal. Sugar gives you energy for an hour, and then you feel tired again.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: Third, try to eat one extra portion of vegetables each day. Not five, just one. It sounds small, but small changes last longer than big promises.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: My biggest mistake was changing everything at once. I stopped sugar, started running and went to bed early, all on the same Monday. By Thursday, I was exhausted and miserable, and I gave up. Now I add only one new habit every two weeks.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: So, choose one thing from today's list and try it. I'd love to hear how you get on.

parts.title: Part 3 · A new runner
parts.intro: You will hear two friends, Chris and Linh, talking about running.

script.speaker: Chris
script.text: Linh, I did it. I signed up for the ten kilometre charity run in October.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Wow, that's brave! Last time we spoke, you said you hated running.

script.speaker: Chris
script.text: I still do, a bit. But my doctor said I should be more active, and a friend said having a goal helps.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: It does. When I trained for my first race, I made a plan and ran three times a week.

script.speaker: Chris
script.text: Three times? I was thinking of every day.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Please don't. That's how people get injured. Run three times, and on other days, walk or swim.

script.speaker: Chris
script.text: OK. Should I buy special shoes?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Definitely. They're the only thing worth spending money on. Go to a proper running shop, and ask them to watch you run.

script.speaker: Chris
script.text: That sounds embarrassing.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: It isn't, honestly. They do it all day. And join a group if you can. I never skip a run when somebody is waiting for me at the park.

script.speaker: Chris
script.text: That's a good idea. Can I join yours?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Of course. We meet at seven on Saturday mornings by the fountain. Don't be late, or we'll leave without you!

parts.title: Part 4 · Healthy Week
parts.intro: You will hear an announcement at a community centre.

script.speaker: Rachel
script.text: Good morning, and welcome to the Riverside Community Centre. This is a message about our Healthy Week, which begins next Monday.

script.speaker: Rachel
script.text: Every morning at seven there will be a free yoga class on the grass behind the centre. If it rains, we'll move indoors to the small hall. Please bring your own mat, or ask at the desk, where we have ten to borrow.

script.speaker: Rachel
script.text: On Tuesday evening, a nurse will give a talk about blood pressure and offer free checks. There's no need to book, but come before six, because the talk starts at half past.

script.speaker: Rachel
script.text: On Wednesday, our café will serve only healthy lunches at half the normal price. The soup of the day is carrot and ginger, which is very popular.

script.speaker: Rachel
script.text: Thursday is Walking Day. We'll meet at the main gate at four o'clock for a walk around the lake. It's about five kilometres, so wear comfortable shoes.

script.speaker: Rachel
script.text: And on Friday, there will be a prize draw for everyone who attended three events. First prize is a year's free membership to our swimming pool.

script.speaker: Rachel
script.text: Finally, sign up for any activity at the front desk or on our website. Thank you, and see you next week.
